rationale: The buyer is a real, named B2B role (HR manager / ops lead at an SMB) already in active vendor evaluation — they've taken demos with Globalization Partners, confirming commercial intent and willingness to spend on EOR. However, this is a low-frequency event per company (an employee relocation happens rarely), which caps pain_frequency and makes recurring revenue difficult to build without broadening scope. Operational autonomy sits at 6 because some light human curation of peer answers or Q&A content would likely be needed to maintain quality, stopping it short of fully autonomous delivery. Validate by testing whether HR ops communities will pay for a structured EOR comparison report or advisory brief.
solution_plan: The micro-service is an on-demand EOR Decision Brief: a structured 8–12 page PDF report (generated by Claude) that compares 3–5 EOR providers on a buyer's specific scenario — country, headcount, tenure situation, and budget. BUILD: the factory sets up a short intake form (Typeform or similar) collecting scenario details, Claude generates the report from a curated provider database, and a Stripe payment link ($79–$149 per report) is embedded on a one-page landing site — no coding by Youval. SELL: reach HR managers via LinkedIn (search 'HR Manager OR People Ops' + company size filters) and post in communities like Reddit r/humanresources and Slack workspaces for HR ops; outreach batches go out only after Youval approves them. MAINTAIN: intake → Claude generation → PDF delivery via email is fully automated; Stripe handles billing; the only recurring human touch is approving outreach batches and updating the provider database (monthly, ~30 min). NOTE: the low-frequency nature of the trigger event means this likely works better as a productized one-time-purchase report than a subscription; validate conversion before building a recurring model.
notes: Does not fail any build_gate outright (all floors met at validate-stage scores), but total of 5.5 sits just at the validate threshold. Primary risk is low event frequency per buyer — this is a one-time pain per relocation, not a recurring workflow, making LTV thin. Needs corroborating signals before advancing.
